# Model card: Message personalisation

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Write the personal paragraph of a candidate message and, for a rejection, one reason sentence from the screening evidence. |
| Workflow | hire |
| Code | `pairly_hire.messaging.drafting` |
| Prompt | `hire_message_draft` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `bd9c9d42dfc3b0a4...` |
| Output schema | `MessageDraft` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 1024 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The template, its purpose, the job title, the language and, for a rejection, the rubric evidence. Never the candidate's name or contact details: the template fills those in.

## Outputs

A `MessageDraft`: `personal_note` and, for a rejection, `reason`.

## Human oversight

`check_draft` refuses unsafe drafts (length, links, contact details, numbers or names not in the inputs, protected characteristics, a reason without evidence). The person edits the text; rejections and offers are sent only after another person approves that exact text.

## Limits

* English and Arabic only.
* A refused draft changes nothing; the person writes the text.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

Structural checks only (`python -m evals.structural`), on the committed recordings: scripted answers, not model output. They say whether every recorded output fits the schema, holds no banned content or em dash, passes the component's own deterministic check and points only at its input. They are not quality judgments: how good a draft is needs a live model and people. The checks also have unit tests.
